product: TREMFYA (guselkumab), with STELARA as the base it is replacing
why_this_product: TREMFYA is J&J's third-largest product (about 5.5% of FY2025 revenue, 10-K FY2025 p.3) and its main replacement for STELARA (U.S. Q3 2026 $1,772M, +79.1%, 8-K 2026-10-13 ex.99.2 p.11). It ties to three findings: gross-to-net (JNJ-c01, c06), the Xoma royalty suit and 5% royalty stack (JNJ-c07), and ICOTYDE cannibalisation inside the same franchise (JNJ-c05). Its U.S. composition patent runs to 2031 (10-K FY2025 p.3), so the label edge has about five years to earn returns.
fine_print_edge: TREMFYA is the only one of the four whose label allows SC induction in Crohn's and UC (400 mg SC at weeks 0, 4, 8; Tremfya label 2.4), while Skyrizi needs 600 mg IV (Crohn's) or 1,200 mg IV over at least two hours (UC) (Skyrizi label 2.6, 2.7), Wezlana needs a weight-based IV infusion (Wezlana label 2.3), and Rinvoq carries a boxed warning and is limited to TNF-blocker failures (Rinvoq label boxed warning, 1.4). In plaque psoriasis TREMFYA is narrower on convenience (every 8 weeks, Tremfya label 2.2, vs Skyrizi every 12 weeks, Skyrizi label 2.3).
